The material designation of the graphite/epoxy composite plate was XAS fibre/914 resin with a layup of (±45/0₂)₃S and dimensions of 73mm x 225mm with a thickness of approximately 2.9mm.
The impact damage was introduced by dropping a 9 kg impactor from a height of 0.5m onto the back face of the clamped specimen.
The C-scan after damage showed the maximum damage occurred at a plane 0.9 of the thickness from the impacted face, with a spanwise length of approximately 40mm.
The frequency response plots showed the modal frequencies were virtually identical between the undamaged and damaged cases, but there were slight differences in relative response amplitudes.
Estimates of modal damping showed an indication that damping increased in the 1050-1150 Hz region after damage, but the authors could not definitively conclude this indicated the presence of damage.
The holographic interferometry results showed perturbations of the fringes near the damage location after impact.

Thermoelastic analysis was only able to obtain suitable stress contours for low frequency modes, due to difficulties in obtaining large enough displacements and stresses at higher frequencies for this specimen.
